The inlet Mach number is set to 2.0 and the Reynolds number based on inlet velocity and axial blade chord is 200,000.
The computational grid has approximately 68,000,000 points, with 1200x280x144 points in the O-grid block and 960x280x72 points in the background Cartesian grid block.
For the adiabatic wall case, the grid resolution in wall units is kept in the range 6 < Δs+ < 25, 0.1 < Δn+ < 0.3, and 3 < Δz+ < 9.
For the isothermal wall simulation, the near-wall grid spacing ranges from 15 < Δs+ < 60, 0.2 < Δn+ < 0.6, and 6 < Δz+ < 19.
The mean separation bubble length is 0.16c_ax for the adiabatic wall case and 0.10c_ax for the cooled wall case.
The skin-friction coefficient distributions show that the separation region is displaced downstream for the cooled wall case compared to the adiabatic wall setup.
A steeper variation of the pressure coefficient is observed downstream of the incident shock for the cooled wall case.
The wall-normal Reynolds stress component is higher for the cooled wall case compared to the adiabatic case.
The shear layer downstream of the separation bubble is more diffused for the adiabatic case, while more concentrated vorticity values are observed when cooling is applied.
For the adiabatic case, the maximum temperature occurs within the separation bubble, while for the cooled wall, higher temperatures are observed along the free shear layer downstream of the bubble.
Before the shock-boundary layer interaction, the location of maximum turbulence amplification is displaced downstream for the cooled wall case.
The same computational grid is used for both the adiabatic and isothermal wall cases, but the near-wall grid spacing has higher values in wall units for the isothermal wall case.
The incident shock wave gets closer to the blade surface when cooling is applied, leading to a steeper variation in the pressure coefficient.
Wall cooling induces the formation of a thinner boundary layer, and the sonic line forms closer to the wall for the cooled wall case.
The separation bubble undergoes a contraction/expansion motion for both the adiabatic and cooled wall cases, with similar excursions from the mean.
